title: STEGO's own code
description: How STEGO's own source is organised and traced, so that the rules STEGO holds generated services to also hold for STEGO: a package belongs to one domain, imports follow the domain order, every file has a record, every test names what it proves, and a stub does not count as built. Decided on 2026-10-31 (the build plan): each rule is met by a predicate of an Assuring specification that assure gate change checks against the base branch, so a change that adds a fault is refused, and gate release refuses any fault at all. The commit and prose conventions that no test can prove stay in AGENTS.md.

title: User docs
description: How STEGO keeps its user docs, such as README.md, current with the product, mechanically. Decided on 2026-11-08: the standard asks for no new doc; it holds the docs that exist to what the spec and the tree say at the same commit, so a change to a command or a path that a doc names shows as a fault in that change.

title: Generator contract
description: How a component's generator must be written, so the same inputs always give the same code. The compiler checks what it can see in a plan (Generating's invariants); these rules cover what only the generator's code can show.

title: Local development
description: Where STEGO's tests run. Decided by the Product owner on 2026-11-05: each thing that STEGO does MUST be testable in a local development environment. This is a core requirement, just below a business outcome. A builder develops against local services, such as PostgreSQL in a local container, and no test needs a shared cluster or a hosted service to prove an obligation. Shared clusters and hosted CI stay for what AGENTS.md keeps them for: performance, stress and scale tests, and a second, platform-level proof. They are never the only proof. The rules serve two outcomes. Evidence for every claim (ST-BO07): a reviewer or an agent can repeat a run at an exact commit only when the run needs no shared system. Consumers feed the registry (ST-BO02): a consumer team can prove a component that it writes without access to the platform's cluster or CI. Each domain follows the pattern ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST, so each rule has a proof in each domain.

title: Domain observability
description: How a generated service reports what happened in its domain. Decided by the Product owner on 2026-11-06: a declared domain probe (ST-DECL-EN20, ST-SUP-RP12) is the only sanctioned path for a fill to emit a log or a domain signal, and log and log/slog are a debug hatch with no contract (ST-EXT-UC01-R06). These rules hold the records and the environments to that decision.

title: Runtime library
description: How the runtime library is written, so that a pinned library with a stable API is not a framework. Decided on 2026-10-29: the code that does not vary with a declaration, such as the outbox queue, the controller loop and tracing, moves out of the generators into one versioned module that generated code imports; 'no runtime dependency on STEGO' becomes 'no framework dependency'. The gain is one copy to audit, smaller generated trees and a smaller generator test matrix; a fix still reaches a service by a registry pin bump and a new run, as a component fix does.

title: Trust and distribution
description: How STEGO is built and shipped so that nothing reaches a generated service without the consumer's verifiable consent. These rules settle the trade between patch latency and the number of artifacts a consumer must trust. They were decided on 2026-10-27 against the alternative of separately releasable generators, which would rebuild the trust model once per generator.

title: Transactional service
description: How a generated service keeps tenants apart, records what happened, decides who may act, survives a retried request, holds money, and shares work between replicas. Decided by the owner on 2026-10-31 in the decision The Transactional Service. Five of the six concerns meet in the one database transaction that the generated store code opens for a write: what is written inside it is atomic with the change, and what is written outside it can be lost on a crash or describe a change that never happened. Tenancy and audit are defaults of every ga archetype; authorization, idempotency and the ledger are bound where a service needs them. The rules here are the ones every component that touches these concerns follows, whatever archetype it is bound into.
